references.text: Mentions Beth-nimrah and Succoth as cities built by the tribe of Gad, the same places mentioned in Joshua 13:27 as part of Gad's inheritance.
Describes Israel's victory over Sihon, king of the Amorites in Heshbon, and the taking over of his kingdom which was later distributed to the tribe of Gad.
Mentions the Sea of Kinnereth (Sea of Galilee) and the Jordan River as geographical boundary markers, the same area described in Joshua 13:27.
Describes Sihon's kingdom with Heshbon as its capital and the areas that were conquered, including the region up to the Sea of Kinnereth.
Provides further description of Sihon's kingdom in Heshbon which was given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
Mentions Succoth as a place east of the Jordan, the same city mentioned in Gad's inheritance in Joshua 13:27.
The first time Succoth is mentioned as a place east of the Jordan where Jacob settled.
Mentions the Sea of Kinnereth as a boundary marker for Israel's land, the same sea that marks the border in Joshua 13:27.
